title: Changing one meeting of a weekly series stores another VEVENT with the same UID

options.label: Bob’s, a guest at one meeting

cases.name: Alice’s change: No other change · Whose copy: Alice’s, the organiser

steps.title: A weekly stand-up is stored as one VEVENT
steps.line: DTSTART is the first meeting; RRULE with COUNT=6 makes six.
steps.caption: Alice’s calendar app saves her stand-up as one VEVENT. DTSTART is the first meeting, Monday 2 November 2026 at 09:00 UTC. RRULE repeats it weekly, and COUNT=6 stops after six meetings, with DTSTART counting as the first. The list shows the meetings a calendar computes from those two lines.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 5 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values.

steps.title: Inviting Bob to one meeting stores a second VEVENT
steps.line: Same UID, and RECURRENCE-ID 20261116T090000Z names the third meeting.
steps.caption: Alice invites Bob to the third meeting only. The app keeps the first VEVENT as it was and adds a second with the same UID, an override. Its RECURRENCE-ID, 20261116T090000Z, is the start the rule gave that meeting. RFC 5545 keeps that value even when the meeting is moved.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 11 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values. Added: 6: BEGIN:VEVENT; 7: UID:standup; 8: RECURRENCE-ID:20261116T090000Z; the override: Week 3: Mon 16 Nov, 09:00, with Bob; and 3 more.

steps.title: Five meetings come from the rule, one from the override
steps.line: The override replaces the start that equals its RECURRENCE-ID.
steps.caption: Alice changes nothing else, so the object keeps two VEVENTs. A calendar takes all six starts from the rule, then puts the override in place of the start that equals its RECURRENCE-ID. Five meetings come from the first VEVENT and one from the second.
steps.picture: Code “Alice’s stored object, some lines left out”, 11 lines; “Meetings Alice’s calendar shows”, 6 labelled values. The master: 1: BEGIN:VEVENT; 2: UID:standup; 3: DTSTART:20261102T090000Z; and 2 more.

steps.title: One UID: at most one master, any number of overrides
steps.line: At a line’s end, a bar is one, a circle zero, a crow’s foot many.
steps.caption: The same storage as a schema. Marks at a line’s ends say how many: a bar is one, a circle zero, a crow’s foot many. RFC 4791 puts every VEVENT with one UID in one calendar object: the master, which it defines as the one without RECURRENCE-ID, and the overrides, which may be stored without it.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 5 entities, 5 relationships.

steps.title: Alice’s copy: two VEVENTs, one UID
steps.line: One master and one override; her calendar shows six meetings.
steps.caption: The server stores Alice’s object as her app saved it: one master with one RRULE and no EXDATEs, and one override, all with UID standup. The notes count each part in her copy, and parts her copy lacks are dimmed. Her calendar shows six meetings.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 5 entities, 5 relationships. Note: “1 master” beside MASTER: DTSTART (datetime); “1 override” beside OVERRIDE: RECURRENCE-ID (datetime), DTSTART (datetime); “1 RRULE” beside RRULE: FREQ (text), COUNT (int); and 1 more.

steps.title: The server refuses a second master or a second RRULE
steps.line: It answers 415; RFC 5545 only says RRULE SHOULD NOT repeat.
steps.caption: Baïkal, running sabre/dav, checks each object saved to it and answers 415 to two VEVENTs without RECURRENCE-ID or to two RRULEs in one VEVENT. RFC 5545 says only that RRULE SHOULD NOT repeat, so here sabre is stricter, and the RRULE line now allows one. Bob’s copy, with no master, is accepted.

two masters: More than one master object was found for the object with UID standup
two RRULEs: RRULE MUST NOT appear more than once in a VEVENT component

two masters: More than one master object was found for the object with UID standup
two RRULEs: RRULE MUST NOT appear more than once in a VEVENT component

steps.picture: ER diagram: 5 entities, 5 relationships. Note: “a second one: 415” beside MASTER: DTSTART (datetime); “a second one: 415” beside RRULE: FREQ (text), COUNT (int). New in this step: MASTER → RRULE: repeats by (each MASTER has zero or one RRULE, each RRULE has exactly one MASTER).
